meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?
Did something happen?
What kind of nonsense is this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
We work better than everyone here.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
And right now excuse me.
Listen, tell me right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: So, will we definitely win right now?
We will definitely punish everyone.
I'll definitely buy you a tank.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.trans: So, will we definitely win right now?
If I win, you will be my servant.

examples.text: Если выиграю я, ты подчиняешься мне.
examples.trans: If I win, you obey me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: We need to give the money to Timur.
Give me just one.
Some water, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.
You two argue really coolly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый').

examples.trans: I came here for a real reason.
Fine, I will go up myself right now.
You yourselves asked for five kilograms.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.trans: We work better than everyone here.
I gave you the very best one.
I meant well, understand.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will'.

examples.trans: And what should I do?
And I do not want to be anyone else.
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh my God.

examples.text: Ну что, Витя, теперь ты мой раб.
examples.trans: Well then, Vitya, now you are my servant.
At least give my office back.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'slave / servant' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вы сможете посмотреть на работу шефа.
examples.trans: You will be able to watch the chef's work.
We work better than everyone here.
Chef, we only do it after work.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Yes, we will pay you well.
Listen to me as a good lawyer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agree').

examples.trans: I agree.
I agree to this bet!

examples.text: Ладно, я согласна на этот план.
examples.trans: Alright, I agree to this plan.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
And start!
Today we have a draw.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of nonsense is this?
This is a service for our guests.
This does not interrupt your rest.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если хочешь их сохранить, не лезь!
examples.trans: If you want to keep them, stay out of my way!

examples.text: Если выиграю я, ты подчиняешься мне.
examples.trans: If I win, you obey me.
Come if you want.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You should introduce a new service.
You are simply spying on me.
Oh, you little macaque monkey!

meanings.en: to obey, to answer to (+ dative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'чиняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to obey, to submit to', paired with 'подчиниться'.

examples.text: И почему мы должны вам подчиняться?
examples.trans: And why must we obey you?
Soldiers obey the commander's order.

examples.text: Как любопытно. И почему мы должны вам подчиняться?
examples.trans: How curious. And why must we obey you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
We are almost there already.
Come on, let's breathe.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: Do not touch our restaurant.
Today the entire restaurant menu is active.
They will buy them at the Chinese restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, let's breathe.
Come on, that is all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'begin', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: And start!
Go ahead and start!
When do I start?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, get ready', paired with 'готовиться'.

examples.trans: Get ready for the procedure.
We got ready to go out.
Arkady Borisovich, prepare for the procedure.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do you have a conscience?
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'started', paired with 'начинать'.

examples.trans: A restroom must be earned first.
Kostya and I started to suspect.
The workday has already started!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'went/am off', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Understand, Vitya, the opening is tomorrow.
Fine, I will go up myself right now.
No, thank you, I will go.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'faster', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!

examples.text: Быстро уберите всех тараканов с кухни!
examples.trans: Quickly remove all the cockroaches from the kitchen!
Right now we will fix everything quickly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'forward', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go, go, faster forward!
Go ahead.

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне нужно доверие, а не ревность.
examples.trans: I need trust, not jealousy.
With them, if you are jealous, it is bad.
Yeah? Come on then, let's go.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: Do not even dare to say that.
What are you talking about at all?

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'which', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.

examples.text: Я как будто в театр сходил.
examples.trans: It is as if I went to the theater.
And how should I react?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
What is with you, mommy, huh?
Oh my God.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'monster' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What a monster you are!

examples.text: Сделайте что-нибудь с этим пьяным чудовищем!
examples.trans: Do something with this drunken monster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: Today we have a draw.
Did they bring the mussels today? No.
I will fire all of you today!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дача'). Common feminine noun meaning 'luck, fortune' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: How do you know? Does it show already?

examples.text: Куда мы спрячем эту большую коробку?
examples.trans: Where will we hide this big box?
Today luck is on my side!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'торона'). Common feminine noun meaning 'side' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Today luck is on my side!
On the other hand, it's interesting.
The shop is on that side.
